correctness.rationale: If every occupied image level contains at least two points, comparability forces each such target level to receive points from exactly one source level and every source level to occur; with equal source and target heights, monotonicity makes this assignment the identity, so the map is level-preserving and nonconstant on every level. Otherwise the image weak order has a singleton occupied level and its order complex is a cone, so the map factors through a contractible image and is null-homotopic. A levelwise nonconstant map acts nontrivially on top rational homology. Any pointwise-comparable map has the same action, hence is also levelwise nonconstant and level-preserving; comparability inside an antichain then forces equality. Fresh enumeration of the (2,2,2) case independently gives 446 maps and exactly nine components, one of size 438 and eight singletons.

final_claim: For a finite weak order with at least three antichain levels, each of size at least two, all self-maps outside the level-preserving levelwise-nonconstant maps form one null-homotopy class, while every such level-preserving nonconstant map is an isolated class; hence the number of self-homotopy classes is one plus the product of the numbers of nonconstant self-functions on the levels.
